title: An object literal at a declared shape takes the declared field types, and an existing value's `int` field does not satisfy a `float` one
scope:
how an `int` value meets a `float` field of a shape: in an object literal written where a shape is
declared, and in a shape value or object that already exists. The general `array<int>` → `array<float>`
widening outside a shape is left to another record.
dependsOnText:
[0036](0036.md) (shape types and object literals), [0007](0007.md) and [0054](0054.md) (the
`int` → `float` widening is the one implicit conversion).

summary.headline: Whole numbers in `float` shape fields
summary.body:
`Point $p = {x: 2};` with `type Point = {x: float};` stores `2.0`, and `$p->x` is a `float`. A
shape value that already exists with an `int` field is not accepted where a `float` field is
needed. Build a new value instead: `{x: $old->x}`.
